title.narrative: Integrated time-bound humanitarian assistance to returnees in Sasiga Woreda, East Wollega zone, Oromia region

description.narrative: ltpgtSasiga Woreda is currently facing a severe humanitarian crisis. This situation has been exacerbated by prolonged conflict, large-scale displacement, and deteriorating public services. Due to its high vulnerability to climate shocks, ethnic violence, and systemic service disruptions, the Woreda has been prioritized as highlighted in recent assessments (PAD Needs Assessment, Oct 2025 MIRA Report, June 2025).ltbrgtThe Woreda has a population of approximately 134,154. The humanitarian situation is critical, characterized by an 8% prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) and a significantly weakened health system, with many facilities currently non-operational. Agricultural livelihoods are under threat from insecurity and disease outbreaks, and 63% of water schemes are out of service.ltbrgtIn response to these challenges, PAD, in collaboration with Nexus Ethiopia and local community-based organizations (CBOs), has developed an integrated project targeting five critical sectors: Agriculture, Health and Nutrition, WASH, Shelter/NFI, and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA). This initiative will incorporate protection measures and aims to enhance access to emergency agricultural inputs, restore essential health services, rehabilitate WASH infrastructure, providenbspshelter repair kits, and deliver MPCA to returnees in consultation with CBOs and government stakeholders.ltbrgtA key aspect of this project is its commitment to local leadership and inclusion. Women-led organizations will co-implement the initiative to ensure that women's perspectives are prioritized. The project will actively engage two local CBOs representing PWDs and a Saving and Support association (Iddir), fostering an inclusive approach that empowers marginalized groups.nbsp ltbrgtDesigned to complement ongoing efforts, particularly the EHF projects in adjacent Woredas within the East Wollega Zone, specifically in Gida Ayana. This proposed initiative will leverage existing staff and operational capacities to enhance cost-effectiveness, maintaining operational costs below 10%. This operational presence will facilitate swift project initiation, ensuring both cost and time efficiency.ltbrgtThe project will allocate 17% of its budget to support people with disabilities and the elderly, while a portion will be dedicated to last-mile humanitarian assistance through CBO partners. Additionally, 25% of the project budget is allocated to women-led local implementing partners with an active operational presence in the area. The project will prioritize cash modalities, providing standalone cash support in the form of Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance. Furthermore, cash-based interventions will be integrated across sectors, specifically in Agriculture for procuring improved seeds and Cash for Labor in the ESNFI sector, aligning with the priorities outlined in the allocation paper and cluster recommendations.ltbrgtThis integrated, time-bound humanitarian assistance project for returnees in Sasiga Woreda will span nine months, from November 1, 2025, to July 31, 2026.nbspThe project aims to reach a total of 32,515nbspindividuals (including 17,545nbspfemales), of these 1,902nbsp(F=974)nbsp are persons with disabilities and elders, with a total budget of USD 700,000. The target appears high due to overlapping support across different sectors. It aligns with the strategic objectives of the 2025 HRP, specifically SO1, SO2, SO4, and SO5, as well as the cluster priorities for Agriculture, Health, WASH, MPC, and ESNFI.nbspltbrgtBy addressing immediate needs while laying the groundwork for early recovery, this project aspires to stabilize affected communities and contribute to long-term development. In conclusion, this integrated project proposal for Sasiga Woreda represents a vital intervention in a region beset by humanitarian crises, emphasizing local leadership, inclusivity, and strategic collaboration that foster resilience and recovery for the future.ltbrgtlt/pgt
